title: Why You Remember Stories Better Than Facts
hook: You will always remember a story more easily than a list of facts.

narration.text: You will always remember a story more easily than a list of facts.
This is due to narrative bias, a fundamental way our brains process information.
Stories give information a structure, a beginning, middle, and end.
This structure provides context, making facts easier to connect and recall.
Isolated facts lack these connections, making them harder for our memory to grasp.
This is why teachers often use stories to help students learn complex topics.
And it is why good marketing uses a compelling narrative, not just bullet points.
Have you noticed yourself remembering information better when it is told as a story?

description: Discover why your brain prefers stories over plain facts and how this 'narrative bias' shapes your memory. Learn the secret behind why some information sticks and other facts just fade away.
topic: Why you remember stories better than facts, explaining the narrative bias in memory.
